title: What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn? 🪐
description:
Imagine a glowing bridge of rock across every sky, there day and night.
A thin line overhead at the equator, a giant rainbow arch farther north, and a shadow that makes winters colder. And scientists think Earth may really have had a ring, about 466 million years ago.

Would you want rings over your house? Tell us in the comments.

#shorts #space #science #earth #whatif
facts_checked: Saturn's rings are mostly chunks of water ice, from smaller than a grain of sand to mountain-sized -> https://science.nasa.gov/mission/cassini/science/rings/ ; https://www.planetary.org/space-images/sunlit-saturn-through-its-rings

An Earth ring this close to the Sun would be rock, not ice (ice would sublimate) -> https://www.space.com/what-if-earth-had-rings.html ; https://discovermagazine.com/the-sciences/what-if-earth-really-did-have-rings

Rings would never rise or set and would be visible day and night -> https://www.space.com/what-if-earth-had-rings.html ; https://gizmodo.com/if-earth-had-a-ring-like-saturn-508750253 ; https://discovermagazine.com/the-sciences/what-if-earth-really-did-have-rings

At the equator the ring is seen edge-on as a thin line overhead; at mid latitudes a giant arch like a rainbow -> https://www.livescience.com/what-if-earth-had-rings.html ; https://gizmodo.com/if-earth-had-a-ring-like-saturn-508750253

The ring's shadow falls on the winter hemisphere, so winters could be colder -> https://www.space.com/what-if-earth-had-rings.html ; https://discovermagazine.com/the-sciences/what-if-earth-really-did-have-rings ; https://newsreleases.sandia.gov/releases/2002/earth-sci-fossil-fuel/ringworld.html

Earth may have had a ring about 466 million years ago; 21 Ordovician craters all lie within 30 degrees of the ancient equator; debris fell over millions of years -> https://www.monash.edu/science/news-events/news/2024/earth-may-have-had-a-ring-system-466-million-years-ago ; https://www.livescience.com/space/earth-once-wore-a-saturn-like-ring-study-of-ancient-craters-suggests

The ring's shadow may have contributed to global cooling (Hirnantian icehouse) - hypothesis, said with 'might' -> https://www.monash.edu/science/news-events/news/2024/earth-may-have-had-a-ring-system-466-million-years-ago ; https://www.livescience.com/space/earth-once-wore-a-saturn-like-ring-study-of-ancient-craters-suggests
